title: Natural finite completed-module model of the affine section-limit functor
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, $I$ a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf, and $V$ an affine open with its Noetherian open subscheme. Put $A=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_X)$, $J=I(V)$, and $\widehat A=\varprojlim_n A/J^{n+1}$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Write $\mathit{Coh}(X,I)$ for the coherent formal modules [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module], $\rho_V$ for their termwise restriction [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-restriction-objects], $\mathrm{Fin}(\widehat A)$ for the full subcategory of finitely generated $\widehat A$-modules, $\iota$ for its inclusion, and $\mathrm{Res}_A^{\widehat A}$ for restriction of scalars. There exists an equivalence $E:\mathit{Coh}(V,I|_V)\simeq\mathrm{Fin}(\widehat A)$ together with a natural isomorphism $L_V\cong\rho_V\circ E\circ\iota\circ\mathrm{Res}_A^{\widehat A}$ (composition in application order), where $L_V(F)=\varprojlim_n\Gamma(V,F_{n+1})$ and $L_V(\alpha)=\varprojlim_n\Gamma(V,\alpha_{n+1})$. This is only the completed-module model, with no kernel, cokernel, exactness or annihilator assertion.

source.place: Lemma 087W (lemma-inverse-systems-affine), its limiting-module construction and natural morphisms, and Lemma 087X (lemma-inverse-systems-abelian), affine reduction; checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/087W and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/087X.

proof.text: Identify the affine open subscheme V with Spec A by IsAffineOpen.isoSpec. The ideal sheaf transported along the inverse isomorphism is ofIdealTop of the ideal J transported along GammaSpecIso. Check this equality on affine sections: the top section-ring map of the canonical affine isomorphism is V.topIso.hom followed by GammaSpecIso.inv; ideal comap along an open immersion is ideal extension along that same map. Thus the resulting ideal is exactly J=I(V), including J=0 and J=A.

Use the actual termwise formal pullback functors for the affine isomorphism and its inverse, including their equalities after the full-subcategory inclusions. Pullback composition and identity natural isomorphisms cancel the two composites; fully faithful cancellation lifts them to formal modules. This constructs a transport equivalence whose underlying functor is the stated termwise pullback, rather than an unspecified abstract equivalence.

Apply coherentFormalModules_affine to A, J and the transported ideal with the equality from step 1. Compose its equivalence with the transport equivalence from step 2 to obtain E. The limiting cones p in that theorem specify the underlying A-module and commute with every morphism of formal modules. Their scalar action is along algebraMap A (AdicCompletion J A).

For every global F, restrict termwise to V. For each level, restrictAppIso identifies its top sections with Gamma(V,F_n); scalar compatibility follows from smul_restrictAppIso_hom and the top-ring maps in step 1. Apply the Spec global-sections scalar transport to those comparisons to identify the entire A-module diagrams. Transport p through that diagram isomorphism, giving a limiting cone over the concrete section diagram. Its unique comparison with limit.cone gives an A-linear isomorphism. Naturality of p and uniqueness of lifts show these object comparisons commute with limit maps for every alpha, so assemble them with NatIso.ofComponents. This proves the asserted comparison after rho_V. Empty V gives only zero modules and the same construction.

proof_origin.place: The natural affine-presentation comparison from Lemma 087W and the affine reduction in Lemma 087X, separated from exactness and annihilator transport.
